title: How to Let AI Agents Sign Up for Your App Safely — Isabelle Williams, WorkOS
talk_summary: A WorkOS PM demos letting AI agents sign up for and act inside a third-party app using the emerging auth.md protocol and ID-JAG identity assertions, plus scoped agent tokens with permission ceilings and revocation. It is about agent-facing auth standards for consumer apps, not about running an internal agent workforce.

takeaways.technique: Scoped agent tokens with permission ceiling (intersection of user perms and agent blueprint)
takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of handing an agent the user's token or a broad API key, the app issues a distinct agent token whose subject is the agent ID and whose scopes are the intersection of the invoking user's permissions and a per-agent blueprint ceiling; the agent cannot exceed the blueprint even if the user could.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the scopes in it is the intersection of Jordan's user permissions and the scopes in the ceiling of the agent blueprint

takeaways.technique: Separate agent identity from user identity for audit and revocation
takeaways.what_they_do: Agent tokens carry the agent ID as subject plus an 'acting on behalf of' claim, so every action is attributable to a specific agent and can be revoked independently of the user's session.
takeaways.evidence_quote: The subject of the agent token is the agent ID, so it's attributable to the actual agent. It's acting on behalf of Jordan the user

takeaways.what_they_do: Host a markdown file at a well-known path that describes how an agent can discover access, register, and call the API, with the app enforcing the actual rules server-side.
takeaways.evidence_quote: It's where an agent can discover how to get started with your application. It describes the mechanisms for getting access
